surprises.head: The Rangers found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Seattle is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: the Rangers’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.2% against Seattle) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Kartye scores in his return to Seattle
paras: This one got way too interesting for the Rangers. Gabe Perreault struck first for the Rangers a minute and a half in. The Rangers had a goal taken off after a video review midway through the first, though it didn’t end up costing them. Tye Kartye pushed the lead to 2-0 on the power play later in the period, in his first game back in Seattle. Jaroslav Chmelař stretched the lead to 3-0 less than five minutes later. Seattle pulled Joey Daccord after three goals and turned to Philipp Grubauer for the rest of the first. Pavel Dorofeyev extended the lead to 4-0 midway through the second, and that one stood up as the winner. Kaapo Kakko and Jordan Eberle scored less than five minutes apart early in the third to cut the Rangers’ lead to 4-2. Vince Dunn made it 4-3 with just under five minutes left, and the Rangers had to hang on.

The Rangers had the better of the chances. Joonas Korpisalo, in his first game since coming over from Boston, made 25 saves for the Rangers. The Rangers improved to 10-7-1, third in the Metropolitan, while the Kraken fell to 9-6-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Rangers.
Berkly Catton has a point in eight straight games.
Jaroslav Chmelař scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 4 (14 games played since).
Alberts Šmits was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Matthew Robertson played instead.
